main_text.p: us carnem odio habuit,imò enutrit ac fouet eam,sicut & Dominus ecclesiam. Quoniam membra sumus corporis eiusde, ex carne eius & ex ossibus eius. Interim tamen observatione dignū, quòd mulier non de pede viri sumpta est, ne à viro conteneretur, 1.Pet.3. neq; de capite, ne viro dominaretur, 1.Tim.2. Si enim maritus vincatur, & uxor dominetur, (dicit Augustinus in Psal.143.) pax perversa est. Si autem uxor marito dominanti subijciatur, pax recta. Io. Iouianus scribit cap.3. de Obed. lib.3. Quænam pax in illa esse domo potest, in qua mulieris dominetur appetitus? Neq;.n.aut induere omnes Scra-tè possunt, aut ducendæ uxoris finis is est viro, ut patientia assuefcat, toleràdisq; clamorib.

Septimó propter unam & eandem spem vocationis, qua & vir & mulier, abs-q; perfo-narum acceptione vocati sunt ad hæreditatem gratiæ vitæ.Ephes.4.1.Pet.3.Si ergo spe-rant coniuges se simul victuros[?] in summa pa-ce & tranquillitate post hanc vitam in regno Dei; cur non etiam hic ad momentum saltem student pacificè viuere? At patientia illis est opus, ut ubi voluntatem Dei peregerint, re-portent promissionem, Hebr. 10. Neque e-nim seruari unquam concordia, nisi per so-lam patientiam valet, sicut Gregorius testa-tu lib. Moral. 5. Crebrò namque in humana actione nascitur, unde mentes hominum vicissim à suavitate & dilectione separen-tur. Et nisi ad adversa toleranda in animo[?]

page.notes: Running head is "NVPTIALES." as printed (the N-V ligature is hard to read exactly). Page number "251": the final numeral is slightly blurred and could be read as "25ı". The "3" in the references "1.Pet.3.", "cap.3.", "lib.3." and "Pet.3." is printed as a yogh-like form (ʒ); transcribed as 3. The word after "vi" in "victuros" has a ligature (ct) that is not fully clear, so it is marked [?]. The last word "in animo" appears as "in snimo"; the first letter looks like an s or a long-s-like form, so it is read as "animo" and marked [?]. The page ends mid-sentence, and the paragraph continues on the next page. Faint scan artefacts (dashes and a small mark) at the very bottom are not printed text and are left out. Text in the scan has u/v and i/j normalised per the convention; long s is written as plain s.
